question: In a patient with unilateral conductive hearing loss, the Weber tuning-fork test lateralises to the affected (poorer) ear.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Weber lateralises to the affected ear in conductive hearing loss (e.g., CSOM, otosclerosis) but to the better ear in sensorineural hearing loss. This distinction is a classic ENT examination trap.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In conductive hearing loss the affected ear is relatively shielded from ambient noise, so bone-conducted sound is perceived louder there — Weber lateralises to the affected side.
